questions.stem: In the Haber process, only about 15% of nitrogen and hydrogen is converted to ammonia in each pass through the reactor. How is a high overall yield still achieved?

options.text: By using a different reaction pathway entirely
By using a very large amount of catalyst
By recycling the unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen back through the reactor

questions.explanation: After each pass, the ammonia is cooled and liquefied (it has a boiling point of -33°C), separating it from the unreacted gases. The unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen are then recycled back into the reactor for another pass. This process is repeated, eventually converting about 98% of the starting materials into ammonia.
